method.sampling: parent polls the child render process tree every 50 ms via /proc: peak RSS sum, peak browser main-process count (browser executable in cmdline, no --type= argument), peak process count, wall time per child-reported phase
method.scenes: Remotion: C05 fixture job (tests/fixtures/modes/powerpoint_graphic, 180 frames, 1920x1080, 30 fps): first still (bundle build included), warm-bundle still, preview render. Hyperframes: the same fixture retargeted to the hyperframes engine: validate (compositions + lint + check), still (snapshot), preview render (CLI workers 1). Peaks are reported per phase from timestamp-aligned samples.
method.encode: standalone ffmpeg libx264 crf 16 yuv420p re-encode of each produced preview, timed and sampled the same way, isolating the encode share of a render
method.disk: artifact byte sizes from the child reports; hyperframes job work dir total after render

uncertainty: RSS sums count shared pages once per process, so tree peaks overstate true unique memory; the overstatement is the safe direction for a budget and is why profiles add a stated margin rather than trimming to the number
50 ms sampling can miss spikes shorter than the interval; the 1.30 profile margin covers this

this box is shared with other build work: wall times are load-dependent and inflate under contention, while RSS peaks are comparatively stable; treat peaks as +/-10 percent and wall times as upper bounds
Remotion still timings depend on the bundle cache state, which the record states explicitly

Hyperframes peaked at multiple Chromium main processes inside one render: the CLI multiplies browsers internally, which is why profiles are sized from whole-tree peaks and the budget counts operations, not browser processes
